hints.title: Manager Hierarchy Traversal
hints.text: Find all employees who report directly or indirectly within three management levels to the head of the company.

hints.title: Self-Join or Recursive CTE
hints.text: Join the employee hierarchy three times, or use a recursive CTE starting from manager_id = 1.

hints.title: Three Level Hierarchy Blueprint
hints.text: with recursive Subordinates as (select employee_id from Employees where manager_id = 1 and employee_id <> 1 union all select e.employee_id from Employees e join Subordinates s on e.manager_id = s.employee_id) select employee_id from Subordinates.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH RECURSIVE Hierarchy AS (
    SELECT employee_id, 1 AS level
    FROM Employees
    WHERE manager_id = 1 AND employee_id != 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT e.employee_id, h.level + 1
    FROM Employees e
    JOIN Hierarchy h ON e.manager_id = h.employee_id
    WHERE h.level < 3
)
SELECT employee_id
FROM Hierarchy;
```

complexity.notes: Recursive expansion descends at most 3 levels, visiting each subordinate employee once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Single join only captures direct reports and omits employees reporting through intermediaries.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Recursive CTE avoids hardcoding multiple nested self-joins.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of recursive CTE or 3-level self-join excluding the head manager.
